title: What if the Moon orbited as low as the ISS? 🌕
subject: moon
description:
Would you want to see it rise just once? 👇

What if the Moon orbited Earth at the same height as the International Space Station? It would fill half the sky, race overhead every 90 minutes, and then get torn apart by Earth's tides.

Sources: Phil Plait, Bad Astronomy (SYFY WIRE, "What if the Moon orbited at the same height as the ISS?"), NASA Moon facts
tags: what if the moon was as close as the iss
what if the moon was closer

scenes.text: The Moon would cover half your sky.
That's if it orbited as low as the International Space Station, 420 kilometers up instead of 384,000.
It would cross the sky in about 5 minutes. Right overhead, it would make you 10 percent lighter.
Astronomer Phil Plait says tides would grow nearly 100,000 times stronger, with floods kilometers high.
Then Earth's tides would rip the Moon apart.
It would end as a thick ring of rock circling Earth.
